parts.text: Brik is a triangle-shaped fried pastry, typically filled with meat or fish and an egg, made from a paper-thin pastry sheet called malsouka. Its origins are unclear: the name may come from the Turkish börek, while one account places its origin in southern Tunisia among Tunisian Jews. Fillings vary by region, such as the Djerba version with potato, parsley and harissa.
Brik is a dish of Tunisian cuisine that is also essential during Ramadan, and the egg yolk inside is kept runny.

blocks.title: Najet Hadriche's Tunisian brik with shrimp
blocks.sub: One version of the dish, as given by The National; the steps are summarised in our own words. Recipes differ from cook to cook.
blocks.note: Makes 20 to 25 rolls. This is a tube-shaped shrimp and tuna variant (asabe Fatima) made with spring roll wrappers in place of malsouka; the common brik is triangular with a whole egg.

ingredients.name: potato, cut into small squares and boiled
shrimp, shelled, cleaned, deveined and chopped

steps.text: Mash the onion, boiled potato and parsley together in a bowl until combined.
Mix in the shrimp and tuna, then the spices, salt and pepper, and finally the beaten egg until everything is evenly blended.

Lay out one wrapper at a time, keeping the rest covered. Put a tablespoon of filling across the centre on the diagonal, fold a corner over it, tuck in the sides and roll it up into a cigar, sealing the end with a drop of water. Repeat until the filling is used up (the rolls can be frozen now and thawed for 15 minutes before frying).
Heat 4 to 5 cm of oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the rolls in batches, turning once halfway, until golden on all sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve straight away with lemon wedges.
